explanation: In the US, tipping 15-20% of the pre-tax bill at a sit-down restaurant is a deeply embedded social norm, not a bonus: federal law lets employers pay tipped workers a direct cash wage of just $2.13/hour (versus the $7.25 federal minimum), with tips expected to make up the difference. Skipping or significantly under-tipping for normal service is widely seen as a breach of etiquette, since servers' income structurally depends on tips.
local_tip: Tip 15-20% of the pre-tax total for sit-down service, and if service was genuinely poor, speak to a manager rather than leaving no tip.

also_check.note: Tipping is not practiced and can be seen as insulting; excellent service is already the baseline expectation.
A service charge is included by law, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.
Tipping is not customary and can confuse or embarrass staff; upscale restaurants may add a service charge instead.
